The best marvel rivals pc build for high FPS pairs a fast gaming CPU with a mid-range or better graphics card, 32GB of DDR5 and a high refresh rate monitor. Marvel Rivals runs on Unreal Engine 5, so it leans harder on hardware than older hero shooters. For smooth 1080p and 1440p play in 2026, an RTX 5060 Ti or RTX 5070 with a Ryzen 7 9800X3D is the sweet spot.

Below are three parts lists – entry, high FPS and maximum – plus the settings that matter most, so you spend money where it actually lifts your frame rate.

Marvel Rivals System Requirements in Plain English

NetEase lists modest minimum specs: a GTX 1060 6GB or RX 580 class graphics card, an Intel Core i5-6600K or Ryzen 5 1600X class processor and 16GB of RAM. The recommended tier steps up to an RTX 2060 Super or RX 5700 XT with a Core i5-10400 or Ryzen 5 5600X. You also need around 70GB of free storage.

Those figures target playable frame rates at modest settings. Competitive players want far more: a steady 144 FPS or higher to match a 144Hz or 240Hz monitor. That target is what the builds below are designed for.

Why the CPU Matters in Marvel Rivals

Team fights in Marvel Rivals are chaotic: twelve heroes, destructible environments, particle-heavy ultimates and constant physics. That load lands on the processor as much as the graphics card. When frames dip during a big fight, the CPU is often the reason, not the GPU.

That is why we pair every high FPS build with a strong gaming CPU. The AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D, with its large 3D V-Cache, is the best gaming processor on AM5 and keeps frame times steadier in busy scenes. A Ryzen 5 or Core Ultra 5 chip is fine for the entry tier, but it will set the ceiling first.

Entry Build: Smooth 1080p on a Budget

An RTX 5060 with a six-core CPU handles Marvel Rivals well at 1080p with sensible settings. Use DLSS in Quality or Balanced mode and drop the heaviest effects, and the game plays smoothly on a 144Hz monitor. The main compromise is the 8GB of video memory, which limits texture quality over time.

If you can stretch, 32GB of DDR5 RAM is the best upgrade at this tier. Unreal Engine 5 games load a lot of assets, and Discord, a browser and recording software all compete for memory while you play.

High FPS Build: The Sweet Spot

This is the build most competitive players should buy. The Ryzen 7 9800X3D removes the CPU bottleneck in big fights, while an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RTX 5070 pushes high frame rates at 1080p and strong results at 1440p. Together they suit a 240Hz 1080p monitor or a 165Hz 1440p panel.

The RTX 5070 is the better pick at 1440p; the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB wins on value and video memory per dinar. Both support DLSS 4 and NVIDIA Reflex, which lowers input latency – something you feel in a fast hero shooter.

Maximum Build: 1440p 240Hz and 4K

For 1440p at 240Hz or 4K with high settings, step up to an RTX 5070 Ti or RTX 5080. At this level the graphics card carries most of the load, but the 9800X3D is still the right CPU because it keeps minimum frame rates high. Budget for an 850W to 1000W ATX 3.1 power supply and a case with strong airflow.

Best Settings for High FPS in Marvel Rivals

  • Upscaling: turn on DLSS (or FSR on AMD cards) in Quality or Balanced mode. It is the largest single FPS gain.
  • NVIDIA Reflex: enable it with Boost for lower latency.
  • Global illumination and reflections: lower these first; they cost the most frames for the least competitive benefit.
  • Shadows and effects: medium keeps visuals clean without hiding enemy abilities in visual noise.
  • Frame cap: cap a few frames below your monitor’s refresh rate for smoother pacing with G-Sync or FreeSync.

Also enable the EXPO or XMP memory profile in the BIOS. Running DDR5 at its rated speed is free performance that many prebuilt PCs leave switched off.

Frequently Asked Questions

What graphics card do I need for Marvel Rivals at 144 FPS?

For 144 FPS at 1080p, an RTX 5060 Ti or RTX 5070 with DLSS enabled is a reliable choice, paired with a strong gaming CPU. An RTX 5060 can get close with lowered settings. At 1440p, the RTX 5070 or RTX 5070 Ti gives far more headroom for steady high frame rates.

Is the Ryzen 7 9800X3D good for Marvel Rivals?

Yes. The Ryzen 7 9800X3D is the best gaming CPU for a Marvel Rivals PC build because its 3D V-Cache steadies frame times during large team fights, where the game leans on the processor. It also stays relevant for years, so a future graphics card upgrade will not be held back.

Is 16GB of RAM enough for Marvel Rivals?

16GB meets the official requirement and runs the game, but 32GB is the better choice in 2026. Marvel Rivals is an Unreal Engine 5 title, and with Discord, a browser and recording tools open, 16GB fills up quickly and can cause stutter. 32GB of DDR5-6000 is the sweet spot for gaming builds.

Does Marvel Rivals need an SSD?

Yes. Install Marvel Rivals on an NVMe SSD. The game needs around 70GB of space, and a hard drive causes slow loading and texture pop-in. A 1TB NVMe drive is the practical minimum for a gaming PC today, and 2TB gives room for several large games alongside it.

Can a gaming laptop run Marvel Rivals at high FPS?

Yes, a laptop with an RTX 5060 or RTX 5070 runs Marvel Rivals well at 1080p, especially with DLSS. Laptops run hotter and throttle sooner than desktops, though, so a desktop gives higher sustained frame rates for the money and is easier to upgrade. Use a cooling pad and keep vents clear.

The Bottom Line

The strongest marvel rivals pc build for high FPS in 2026 is a Ryzen 7 9800X3D with an RTX 5060 Ti 16GB or RTX 5070, 32GB of DDR5-6000 and a fast NVMe SSD. Go entry level with an RTX 5060 for 1080p, or step up to an RTX 5070 Ti or RTX 5080 for 1440p 240Hz and 4K. Turn on DLSS and Reflex, lower global illumination first, and enable EXPO.
